extracted.intended_audience: Navy and Marine Corps public affairs officers, commanders, event planners, and staff responsible for civilian embarkations, aerial events, ship ceremonies, exhibits, and music program coordination
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and operational criteria for planning, approving, and conducting Department of the Navy public affairs events including civilian guest embarkations, naval aerial events, ship ceremonies, national observances, exhibits, and military music participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation contents and guest pre-embarkation information
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information should be included or provided by separate letter: recommended wardrobe, passport and immunization requirements, availability of emergency medical and dental facilities and ship’s store and other facilities available; address use of personal cameras; statement of fund reimbursement policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanding officer should enumerate camera restrictions once guests arrive; commanding officer is responsible for control of photography. Include emergency facility availability and other practical details so guests can plan; include specific reimbursement policy wording (see policy quote).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund reimbursement policy disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of the Navy has no specific authority to use its funds to defray or reimburse a Navy guest for his or her personal expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly inform guests they must provide their own transportation to/from embarkation and be prepared to meet any extraordinary expenses (e.g., commercial transportation home if leaving early). State that meals aboard will be nominal and that guests should be prepared to cover personal emergency travel costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety/hazard warning and acceptance condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Navy ships and aircraft present certain hazards not normally encountered ashore and require persons on board to exercise a high degree of care for their own safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a statement that "Acceptance of this invitation will be considered your understanding of the above limitations and arrangements." Use this to ensure guests acknowledge inherent hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest financial responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests are responsible for providing their own transportation to and from their residences and must reimburse the Navy for living and incidental expenses because programs are conducted at no additional cost to the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear in invitations/briefings that participation is at no additional cost to the government and that guests should plan to cover incidental/personal expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest selection criteria — civic/professional involvement and DV definition
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the criteria in guest selection is the extent of involvement in civic, professional and social organizations; a Distinguished Visitor (DV) is an individual who has not had substantial previous exposure to the Navy and who has a wide sphere of influence in their profession/community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize nominees with broad influence (e.g., top-level executives, school principals, teachers); spouses/family members should not normally be included unless they qualify as DVs; ensure participant diversity in racial and ethnic backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic/itinerary rules for embarkations
rubrics_metrics.description: Atlantic embarks on ships operating between East Coast ports or CONUS and U.S. Caribbean; Pacific embarks on West Coast, CONUS-Hawaii/Alaska, intra-Hawaii/Alaska, or Mexico/Canada case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If embarkations begin/end in foreign countries, guests are responsible for passports, visas, and travel requirements. Follow theater-specific constraints when planning embark locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security briefings and photography control
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests will be informed of security restrictions in pre-departure or welcome aboard briefings; unclassified photography should be permitted but guests will be advised of prohibited areas and restrictions will be courteously enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanding officers should include security measures and emergency actions in briefings; enumerated photography restrictions may be issued aboard and enforced by the commanding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Billeting and mess arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests will generally be billeted in officers’ berthing if space permits and normally subsist in the wardroom; guests need not be assigned separate rooms and should be invited to dine at least once in each mess aboard if itinerary permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan billeting and dining to integrate guests into ship routines without unnecessary separate accommodations; schedule at least one dining opportunity in each mess when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest privileges (laundry, ship’s store, NEX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests should generally be afforded privileges of an appropriate mess, use of the ship’s laundry, and ship’s store privileges. Navy Exchange privileges determined case-by-case, limited to emergent needs and items of immediate personal use and souvenirs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit onboard retail privileges to essentials and souvenirs; determine NEX access on a case-by-case basis to avoid improper benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency medical and dental care and notification procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency medical and dental care will be provided when convenient civilian care is not available; in event of injury/serious illness commanding officers will notify operational commanders, CHINFO and cognizant area coordinator by message to OJAG WASHINGTON DC (and DIRPA if Marines involved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanding officers must follow notification chains; if emergency not covered by regulations report facts/circumstances by message to SECNAV with information copies to concerned commands and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Side trips and souvenirs
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests may be allotted time for side trips at their own expense when itinerary includes a port call; as a souvenir of the embark, guests may be provided with a photograph of the ship, suitably inscribed or other memento prior to departure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow reasonable side-trip time at guest expense; provide modest, appropriate mementos such as inscribed ship photographs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public release and media handling for guest embarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Public release about guest embarks will be limited to those initiated by participants; Navy-originated releases will be avoided unless requested by participants. Media queries will be answered fully, stressing that no cost to the government is incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect participant-initiated publicity wishes; be transparent with media about purpose and government cost status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of guests who are members of the news media
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests who are members of the news media will be treated as though present in a news-gathering capacity, and questions and discussions will be handled in accordance with standard requirements governing release of information to news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle media guests under normal news release policies; ensure appropriate coordination and restrictions consistent with security.

rubrics_metrics.name: JCOC (Joint Civilian Orientation Conference) coordination and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: CHINFO is designated to plan and coordinate the Navy phase of the JCOC and evaluate/process nominations originating within the Navy; DIRPA has cognizance over Marine Corps phase; CHINFO/DIRPA may delegate planning; specific guidance on selection criteria/procedures promulgated in advance by CHINFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow CHINFO/DIRPA instructions for nominations and selection; adhere to disseminated selection criteria and coordination rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: DV Embark management and feedback requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CHINFO will maintain list of prospective guests and forward nominations; fleet commanders provide oversight; host ships must submit brief feedback after completion including name of ship, actual embark/debark times and places, names of guests (noting early departures), and relevant events/lessons learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain nomination lists and waiting lists; hosts should provide timely, concise feedback to chain of command and CHINFO with the enumerated items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain of command recordkeeping and coordination responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: CHINFO and DIRPA maintain lists of prospective guests; fleet and other commanders maintain lists of potential guests and those awaiting embarks; coordinate embarks thoroughly; keep electronic records and logs of guests for at least five years; advise CHINFO, DIRPA and concerned commanders when nominees are scheduled to embark; comply with this instruction and applicable directives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accurate, secure recordkeeping for at least five years; coordinate across chain of command and follow instruction when scheduling and managing embarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: DON aerial support policy and DD Form 2535 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: DON aviation asset support of public events shall be in the best interests of DON and performed at no additional cost to the government; a request via DD Form 2535 (Request for Military Aerial Support) shall be submitted for approval to CHINFO or DIRPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All aerial support requests must be documented on DD Form 2535 and routed to CHINFO/DIRPA to ensure conformity with DOD directives and benefit to the Armed Forces; local PAOs may assist but sponsor signs the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility determination for aerial support and mutual-interest requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: CHINFO will be responsible for determining eligibility of Naval Aviation Support requests; off-base aerial events must be of mutual interest to the sponsor and DON and supported at no additional cost to the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate mutual benefit to DON and sponsor; deny or require modification if conditions would impose additional government cost or not align with DON interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aerial support request procedural steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must be submitted to CHINFO Aviation Support Officer or DIRPA Aviation Coordinator using DD Form 2535; sponsor must complete and sign; local PAOs/recruiters/aviators may assist administratively but shall not submit on behalf of sponsor; local commanders share concerns; FAA safety inspector review required for non-static displays; include site certification signed by FAA agent; once eligible CHINFO assigns event number and notifies sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow each step strictly; ensure FAA approvals and site certifications are obtained prior to submission for non-static events; maintain clear coordination with local commanders and CHINFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aerial support submission deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: No exceptions except for unavoidable high-profile events. Static displays: submit at least 5 working days before event; Flyovers: at least 10 working days; Air shows: at least 45 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to deadlines to allow safety and coordination reviews; only rare, unavoidable circumstances justify exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flyover limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Flyovers are limited to a maximum of four aircraft from the same military service of the same type making one non-maneuvering pass over a fixed point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan flyovers to conform to this maximum and to be non-maneuvering; requests exceeding this must follow higher-level approval rules (see aerial reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing man formation authorization and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing man formations are authorized for solemn commemorative ceremonies (Memorial Day, POW/MIA Recognition Day, Veteran’s Day and similar events) and shall not be performed at CONUS public events without prior SECNAV approval except for funerals; approved for specified categories of deceased (active duty aeronautically designated officers, personnel dying in aviation-related accidents, certain trainees, flag officers, war heroes, dignitaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit missing man formations to appropriate solemn contexts and approved personnel categories; obtain SECNAV approval for CONUS public events except funerals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Static display staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: When an aircraft is on display, DON members must be on hand to help observers and to answer questions about aircraft mission, performance and Navy recruiting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure knowledgeable DON personnel are present to engage the public and support recruiting objectives during static displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blue Angels scheduling and submission timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Blue Angels normally limit performances to air shows; DD Form 2535 must be submitted to the CHINFO Aviation Support Officer by August 1 of the year prior to the year of the air show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the advanced submission date for Blue Angels appearances and coordinate scheduling well in advance due to limited performance slots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single aircraft tactical demonstration eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: CHINFO is responsible for determining eligibility of tactical demonstration aviation support requests; single aircraft demonstrations showcase specific capabilities and flight characteristics of DON aircraft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit requests and justification for tactical demonstrations to CHINFO; demonstrations should focus on capability display without imposing extra cost or unsafe conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aerial review restrictions and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Aerial reviews (a flyover of more than four aircraft, or of multiple types of aircraft, or of aircraft representing more than one Military Service) are reserved for the most meaningful occasions and shall not be performed at CONUS public events without prior approval ASD(PA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit aerial reviews to highly significant events; obtain ASD(PA) approval for CONUS events and submit via DD Form 2535.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aerial events on DOD installations approval threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: CHINFO is responsible for approving aerial events connected to open houses, base air shows, and other events open to the public and news media; aerial events that support small or by-invitation-only ceremonies with limited or no media exposure do not require CHINFO approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine approval needs based on public/media exposure; coordinate with CHINFO for public-facing aerial events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for official function participation and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders may authorize participation in official government, military and civic functions except those in the National Capital Region; definitions provided for official government, official military, official civic and unofficial functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use definitions to evaluate proposed participation; if an event will be televised or receive broad media coverage obtain approval from CHINFO, DIRPA or ASD(PA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance and conduct restrictions at official functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Naval personnel who represent the Government must observe the highest ethical standards with strict limits on attendance and conduct, especially when defense contractors are present; avoid conflicts of interest, actual or perceived, and avoid accepting gratuities, gifts or invitations that create appearance issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce JER standards; train attendees on limits and ensure compliance to prevent ethical breaches or perceptions of favoritism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inaugural parades and ceremonies participation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation by active and reserve units is appropriate subject to capabilities and at no additional cost; authorized participation normally limited to a color guard, a brief patriotic opener by a DON band, or a flyover if approved; unauthorized: use of military personnel as escorts, ushers, doormen or drivers for non-military guests or local dignitaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit roles to ceremonial/representational elements; do not provide military personnel for civilian escort or service roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ship ceremony roles, responsibilities and information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: NAVSEA and PEO advise ASN(RD&A) and develop Congressional/DV invitation lists; CHINFO coordinates with OLA to keep SECNAV informed; PCUs coordinate event planning and inform CHINFO, NAVSEA and other commands of dates and updates, including specific information (date, location, times, project officer contact, nearest airport, program availability, principal speaker info). SUPSHIP arranges transportation and approves invitational travel orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow defined coordination lines; include full event details in initial reports and updates; document communications by email and confirm telephone reports by email. Ensure SUPSHIP and NAVSEA consultation for guest lists and logistical arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaker selection and nomination rules for ship ceremonies
rubrics_metrics.description: PEO or builder chooses speakers for christenings; for commissionings PCUs submit principal speaker nominations to CHINFO at least 90 days prior, including biography and justification; reimbursement of speaker's expenses arranged by SUPSHIP; final selection and notification by SECNAV; PCUs must not inform potential speakers they are under consideration; invitations originate from CHINFO or DIRPA under SECNAV signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit nominations early with supporting info; do not pre-notify candidates; follow SECNAV/CHINFO/DIRPA protocols for formal invitations and expense arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keel laying and launching public announcement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Keel laying ceremonies authorized only under unique circumstances; public announcement of keel laying shall not be made more than two months before the ceremony; clear releases with regional and area coordinators and simultaneous release through ASD(PA), OLA and other offices as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit early publicity for keel layings; coordinate releases through appropriate offices to manage public messaging and congressional relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioning, recommissioning and decommissioning planning timelines and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: PCU advises CHINFO at least six weeks prior to commissionings; ORF may be requested under certain circumstances for first commissionings, recommissionings or unique missions; decommissionings may be significant and NAVSEA will advise CHINFO six weeks prior; guest lists compiled by commanding officers in consultation with NAVSEA and fleet/type/regional commanders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan ceremonies with at least six-week lead time for CHINFO notification; evaluate ORF eligibility and funding sources; coordinate guest lists with NAVSEA and relevant commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ship ceremony funding policy and in-kind donation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Keel layings and launchings normally funded by building yard; commissionings funded by DON; costs exceeding normal operating expenses may be partnered with community; comptrollers and staff judge advocates must advise commander concerning in-kind donations and other gifts; receptions for changes of command usually at expense of outgoing commanders; ORF authorized only through exception to policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess funding source early; obtain legal and comptroller advice on gifts and donations; do not assume ORF availability without exception approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: National and traditional observances participation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for special assistance beyond command capabilities forwarded to CHINFO or DIRPA regional/type/fleet commander with justification via DD Form 2536; participation coordinated by ASD(PA); commands will normally participate using resources at hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit DD Form 2536 for assistance requests; plan observances with available local resources and coordinate early with ASD(PA) coordinators when multi-service or national-level coordination is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint coordination for multi-service observances
rubrics_metrics.description: In observances involving more than one Military Service, ASD(PA) will assign a DOD executive agent or primary coordinator and regional coordinators; regional and installation PAOs should contact coordinators early to integrate command activities with the region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage assigned coordinators early in planning to ensure integration and avoid duplication or conflicts among services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Armed Forces Day and other observance content guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: ASD(PA) announces the theme; CHINFO and DIRPA may issue materials; local command observances should highlight DON’s unique contribution and focus on diverse audiences unfamiliar with DON; COMREL events beyond public visitation should provide meaningful, factual information to target audiences; aerial and other events requested via DD Form 2536.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design observance activities to communicate DON mission and value to target audiences; use provided themes and materials; submit DD Form 2536 for aerial/other support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation limits for service-unique commemorations (birthdays, Navy Day)
rubrics_metrics.description: Navy and Marine Corps birthdays are largely internal; participation voluntary and at attendee's own expense; unit participation for Navy Day is not authorized beyond a brief patriotic opener; public observances must be mutual interest at no additional cost to DON and forwarded to CHINFO via DD Form 2536 if proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep service-unique celebrations internal or limited; ensure any public-facing observance is justified, mutual interest, and funded without extra cost to government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits request timing and neutrality policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits generating national or corporate interest must be requested 90 days in advance via CHINFO or DIRPA and must not favor or endorse in fact or appearance a single commercial entity, group, profit or nonprofit corporation, sect, religious organization, fraternal or political organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit exhibit requests well in advance and design exhibits to be neutral and non-endorsing. Coordinate with supplemental guidance and cognizant approval authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruiting considerations for exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits expected to generate national or corporate interest must be approved via CHINFO or DIRPA (90 days advance) and will be routed for ASD(PA) approval if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure exhibits intended to support recruiting follow approval channels and timelines; include recruiting objectives in requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency and overseas exhibit approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Overseas and international exhibits of the U.S. Government will be approved by ASD(PA) via CHINFO and DIRPA and normally will not result in additional costs to DOD; overseas commands forward requests via the combatant commander; foreign trade show approvals involve Defense Security Cooperation Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Route international exhibit requests through combatant commander and CHINFO/DIRPA; anticipate interagency and security coordination and avoid additional DOD costs where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naval music program — program purpose and competition restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Military musical participation in public events that meet other criteria is limited to patriotic programs as opposed to pure entertainment; military musicians will neither be placed nor place themselves in competition with civilian musicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit music participation to patriotic/community-interest contexts and avoid competing with civilian entertainers; consult supplemental guidance for permitted/forbidden participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naval music program — authorized participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized participation includes music to accompany presentation of national colors or performance of military/patriotic music by band/drum/choral groups; music for public events and parades open to entire community; music for events that charge admission if the band's performance is incidental and no additional charge to hear the band.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approve band participation where patriotic purpose and public/community access are primary; ensure there is no separate charge to hear military musical performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naval music program — unauthorized participation
rubrics_metrics.description: DON musicians are not authorized to provide entertainment at luncheons, dinners, receptions, dances, or other functions in the civilian domain attended primarily by persons not on active duty; background or social music considered entertainment and not authorized; commercial sponsorships or events tied to religious/ideological/partisan politics are not authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deny requests that amount to entertainment or commercial/political endorsement; require event sponsors to certify no conflict with local civilian musicians and attach union statement when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music program requests and coordination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective civilian sponsors must submit requests for musical participation via DD Form 2536 and certify no conflict with local civilian musicians (attach a statement from the local musicians' union); Navy Bands coordinate with CHINFO and Marine Bands with DIRPA for events involving multiple bands, national/international importance, national sports/professional athletic events, national TV/radio events, OCONUS travel, or any request that does not meet normal conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require sponsor certifications and union statements; route unusual or high-profile music requests through CHINFO/DIRPA and obtain necessary approvals before committing bands.
